name: Foodie Long Weekend
anchorStayBlurb: Jackalope Hotel at Merricks North is on the Willow Creek Vineyard estate. The on-site Doot Doot Doot restaurant and the cellar door mean the accommodation is part of the gastronomic experience, not just a bed between meals. Sunday morning is an on-site cellar door visit before departure.
intro: Two nights at Jackalope built around a Saturday morning Peninsula produce trail, a small-group guided cellar door tour in the afternoon, and a degustation dinner on Saturday evening. The day moves deliberately from raw produce to estate wine to the kitchen's interpretation of both.
whyThisCombination: The Peninsula has a density of food and wine producers per square kilometre that most Australian regions cannot match, but accessing that density requires a sequencing solution that wine-focused packages typically ignore. The morning is produce and provenance: the Saturday market and a producer visit, where the conversation happens with the person who made the thing you are eating. The afternoon is guided wine: a small-group tour at premium family-owned estates where the emphasis on food alongside wine is the differentiating feature. The evening is the chef's table: the arrival point that the whole Saturday has been building towards. The Jackalope anchor is the specific argument: a design hotel on a working vineyard where Sunday morning can be spent at the on-site cellar door rather than driving to a separate property. For a food-and-wine audience, the accommodation being part of the gastronomic experience rather than incidental to it is a meaningful consideration.
bookingSequence: Book Jackalope first, 8 to 10 weeks ahead for peak weekends. Book the degustation at Doot Doot Doot immediately after confirming the stay - the Saturday evening chef's table is time-sensitive and is the culminating experience the whole Saturday builds towards. Book the guided cellar door tour after the degustation is confirmed. Confirm the produce trail details last: check whether the Red Hill Market falls on your chosen Saturday (it runs the third Saturday of each month only) and arrange the producer visit with any advance contact required.

faq.question: What if the Red Hill Market isn't running on our Saturday?
faq.answer: The Red Hill Consolidated School Market runs the third Saturday of each month. If your chosen weekend does not align, substitute a self-guided produce route through the Red Hill corridor: Red Hill Estate cellar door and kitchen, a local providore, and a coffee at a Red Hill area cafe. The Saturday structure still works; the market is the ideal version, the substitute is functional.

faq.question: Can the full-day wine tour be adapted to an afternoon-only session to allow for the morning market?
faq.answer: A full-day tour operator and a Saturday morning produce trail cannot occupy the same day. The solution is to book a flexible-timing operator such as Rick's Wine Tours for the afternoon cellar door component, or to move the produce trail to Friday afternoon and run the full-day tour on Saturday. Confirm the timing configuration with the tour operator before booking.

faq.question: Is Peninsula Insider the booking agent for this package?
faq.answer: No. Peninsula Insider is an editorial publisher. Each component is a direct transaction with its operator. Peninsula Insider provides no booking guarantee or customer service for any component.
